memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When human beings began to increase in number on the earth and daughters were born to them, the sons of God saw that the daughters of humans were beautiful, and they married any of them they chose. - Gen 6:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the more mysterious passages in Genesis, and sincere believers have understood the "sons of God" in different ways. But whatever the exact identity, the heart of the matter is clear: boundaries God set were being crossed. People "married any of them they chose" - the emphasis falls on unrestrained human desire, taking whatever the eye found beautiful, with no thought for God's will.

It echoes the very first sin. Eve "saw that the fruit... was pleasing to the eye" and took it (Gen 3:6). Here again, seeing leads to taking, desire overrules obedience. When a society stops asking "What does God want?" and starts asking only "What do I want?", corruption follows quickly.

We live in a world that celebrates exactly this - following your desires wherever they lead, treating every longing as a right to be satisfied. But not every desire should be acted upon. Some of God's greatest gifts to us are His boundaries, which protect us from ourselves.

The gospel does not ask us to kill desire but to submit it to God, who reshapes what we long for. In Christ, we learn to say with Jesus, "not my will, but yours be done" (Luke 22:42). True freedom is not doing whatever we choose, but wanting what God wants.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are there desires you are treating as rights instead of submitting to God?
- Where do you need to honour a boundary God has set?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me that not every desire should be followed. Reshape my longings, and help me want what You want, as Jesus did.
